quizName: DMV Practice Test #15 25 Questions • Passing Score 21

questions.question: When riding in a group, you should:

options.text: Place inexperienced riders at the back of the group.
Keep enough space between you and other riders.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep enough space between you and other riders.
questions.explanation: When riding in a group, use a staggered formation. Check your mirrors often to see riders behind you. The lead and sweep riders should be experienced. Always keep proper space between all riders in the group.

questions.question: Each traffic lane gives a motorcyclist how many paths of travel?
questions.correctAnswerText: Three
questions.explanation: Each traffic lane has three paths for motorcyclists: left, center, and right.

questions.question: Motorcycle riders:

options.text: Should always wear hearing protection to prevent hearing damage.
Should only wear hearing protection on long rides.
Should not wear hearing protection because it blocks horns and sirens.
Do not need hearing protection if they wear a helmet.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should always wear hearing protection to prevent hearing damage.
questions.explanation: Wind and engine noise can cause permanent hearing damage, even with a full-face helmet. Earplugs protect your hearing while still letting you hear important sounds like horns and sirens.

questions.question: In hot weather, wearing a riding jacket:

options.text: Helps protect against heat exhaustion and dehydration.
Should be avoided because it causes heat problems.
Should only be worn if it is light colored.

questions.correctAnswerText: Helps protect against heat exhaustion and dehydration.
questions.explanation: Wear a riding jacket and long pants in hot weather. They protect you from heat exhaustion and dehydration, in addition to other safety benefits.

questions.question: If a friend has been drinking and wants to drive, which should you NOT do?

options.text: Ask other friends to talk them out of driving.
Tell them to take less-crowded roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell them to take less-crowded roads.
questions.explanation: To prevent drunk driving, arrange other transportation, get other friends to help talk them out of it, and slow their drinking. Never let them drive, no matter what roads they take.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Slow or stop
questions.explanation: When the left arm is bent at the elbow and pointing downward, it means the rider is slowing down or stopping.

questions.question: A child passenger:

options.text: Should sit in front of the operator.
Does not need to reach the footrests.
Should hold onto the motorcycle frame.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should sit behind the operator.
questions.explanation: A child should always sit right behind the operator. A child in front may not balance well and could get in the way of the controls.

questions.question: When turning a three-wheeled motorcycle through a curve, it is best to:

options.text: Stay in the center of the lane.
Stay on the outside of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change your path as needed.
questions.explanation: Three-wheeled motorcycles corner differently than two-wheeled ones. The best path through a curve may not follow the curve exactly. You may need to move from the outside to the inside of the curve before straightening out.

questions.question: To swerve correctly:

options.text: Press the handgrip in the direction you want to turn.
Press the handgrip in the opposite direction of your turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handgrip in the direction you want to turn.
questions.explanation: To swerve, press the handgrip on the side you want to turn. Press the opposite handgrip to go back to your original direction once you are clear of the hazard.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a good safety tip?

options.text: Slow to a safe speed before turning.
When turning, lean in the direction you want to go.
Avoid dragging your feet on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid looking at other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Always slow down before turning and lean in the direction of the turn. Do not drag your feet as they could catch on something. Always watch for other traffic on the road.

questions.question: When packing a load on a motorcycle, where should heavier items go?
questions.correctAnswerText: Toward the front
questions.explanation: Place heavier items toward the front of the load. Loads should be over or in front of the rear axle. Pack lighter items behind you.

questions.question: How should you park a motorcycle next to a curb?

options.text: At a 90-degree angle with the rear wheel touching the curb
At a 45-degree angle with the front tire touching the curb
Like a car, with both wheels the same distance from the curb
At the left edge of the space so drivers can see it better

questions.correctAnswerText: At a 90-degree angle with the rear wheel touching the curb
questions.explanation: Park your motorcycle at a 90-degree angle to the curb by touching your rear wheel to the curb.

questions.question: When riding in a traffic lane, what position should a motorcycle rider use?

options.text: Always ride in the same part of the lane
Change your position based on road and traffic conditions
Always ride in the center of the lane
Always ride in the left part of the lane

questions.correctAnswerText: Change your position based on road and traffic conditions
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always best. Change your position based on the current road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, which part of the lane should you ride in?
questions.correctAnswerText: The center
questions.explanation: When being passed, ride in the center of your lane. Riding on the side nearest the passing vehicle risks a collision. Riding on the far side may encourage the driver to re-enter your lane too soon.

questions.question: What is found in the center portion of a lane?

options.text: It is always the best part of the lane for a motorcycle
Oil and grease, but it is usually safe for riding
Oil and grease, and it is never safe for riding
It is the smoothest part of the lane

questions.correctAnswerText: Oil and grease, but it is usually safe for riding
questions.explanation: Oil drips from cars collect in a strip down the center of each lane. Unless the road is wet, this area usually has enough grip for motorcycles to ride safely. Avoid large buildups of oil and grease found at busy intersections or toll booths.

questions.question: To carry a passenger, which adjustment is not needed?
questions.correctAnswerText: Brake light position
questions.explanation: A motorcycle with a passenger will sit lower due to extra weight. You may need to adjust tire pressure, suspension, shocks, headlight, and mirrors. The brake light position does not need adjustment.

questions.question: Which is not a benefit of riding in a close group?

options.text: It takes up less space on the highway
The group is easier to see
The group is less likely to get separated
Riders reach their destination faster in a close group

questions.correctAnswerText: Riders reach their destination faster in a close group
questions.explanation: Riding in close ranks is better than a spread-out group because it uses less road space, is easier for others to see, and is less likely to get separated. Speed is not affected by how close together riders are.

questions.question: When it starts to rain, what should you do?

options.text: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars
Ride in the center of the lane

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars
questions.explanation: The center of a lane is especially dangerous when wet. When rain starts, avoid the center by riding in the tire tracks left by cars. The left tire track is often the best choice.

questions.question: When it is raining, what is the best thing to do?

options.text: Ride in the center of the lane
Pull off to the side until the rain stops
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars
questions.explanation: When rain starts, the road is especially slippery because oil from cars has not yet washed away. It is safest to ride in the tire tracks left by cars. The left tire track is often your best choice, but this may vary.

questions.question: When riding, what should you do when going through turns?

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders to look through turns
Keep your knees away from the gas tank
Turn only your head and eyes to look where you are going

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head and eyes to look where you are going
questions.explanation: When turning, look through the turn by turning only your head and eyes. Keep your knees against the gas tank for balance. Your arms should be slightly bent when holding the handgrips.

questions.question: When following a car, where should you ride in the lane?
questions.correctAnswerText: The center.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of the lane behind a car. The driver will see you in the rearview mirror. Drivers check their rearview mirror much more often than side mirrors. This position makes you more visible.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: What formation is best for a group of riders entering a curve?
questions.correctAnswerText: Single-file
questions.explanation: Use a single-file formation when taking curves, turning, or entering or exiting a highway. A staggered formation is good for staying close while maintaining safe distance on straight roads.

questions.question: What can increase fatigue while riding?

options.text: Starting a ride late in the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riding in cool weather.
questions.explanation: Dress to protect yourself from tiring weather like wind and rain. Limit riding to about six hours per day. Take a break at least every two hours. Do not use artificial stimulants, as you will feel very tired when they wear off.

questions.question: When planning a long group ride, which idea should you NOT use?

options.text: Plan travel segments based on the least experienced rider.
Skip breaks to reach your destination faster.
Place inexperienced riders behind the leaders.

questions.correctAnswerText: Skip breaks to reach your destination faster.
questions.explanation: Plan routes based on the least experienced rider's skill level. Take regular breaks to reduce fatigue. Place inexperienced riders behind leaders so experienced riders can watch them. Use a staggered formation.
